# ADR 0016 — Only skills that open one of the maintainer's windows are closed to the model

> **In short.** In the context of skills that act outside the repo, facing a rule that would close every such skill
> to the model and with it the whole feature flow, we decided to close only the skills that open a window of the
> maintainer and against closing every skill with an outside side effect, to keep the flow usable while the guards
> hold what it writes, accepting that a flow skill can be started by the model at all.

## Context and problem

ADR 0010 point 7 says a skill with a side effect outside the repo carries `disable-model-invocation`. The flow skills
of ADR 0002 (`plan`, `ticket`, `code`, `comment-audit`) write to Jira and open pull requests. With the line, the model
cannot load them, and the flow from product plan to merged card stops. The line was written for `push` and
`unblock`, which open the maintainer's push and unblock windows.

## Decision drivers

- The model must be able to follow the feature flow it is ordered to run.
- An approval of the maintainer must never be something the model can give itself.
- What a flow skill writes outside the repo is already held by hooks.

## Considered options

- **A — Close only the skills that open a window of the maintainer.**
- **B — Close every skill with a side effect outside the repo.**

## Decision

Chosen: **A**, because B stops the flow while adding no protection the hooks do not already give.

1. **A skill that opens a window of the maintainer or lifts a guard carries `disable-model-invocation`.** Today
   these are `push` and `unblock`; a new skill of that kind gets the line before it is committed. `[Skill push ·
   Skill unblock · Gate check-skills]`
2. **Flow skills stay open to the model, and what they write runs under the guards.** In Progress and Done are held
   by the transition hooks, merges and `main` by `guard-state`, the pull request by `gate-before-pr`, and the build
   starts only on the maintainer's order. `[Hook guard-inprogress · Hook guard-done · Hook guard-state · Hook
   gate-before-pr]`

### Consequences

- Good, because the flow of ADR 0002 runs as ordered.
- Good, because the windows stay the maintainer's alone.
- Bad, because a flow skill can be loaded by the model without an order; the hooks stop what it would write, the
  order itself is a judgment.

### Confirmation

`probe-hooks` turns a forged push or unblock window red, `probe-commands` rejects running the window hooks by hand,
and `check-skills` keeps every skill on its template.

## Rejected

- **B — close every skill with an outside side effect.** The model could not load the flow skills, and the flow of
  ADR 0002 would stop at its first step.
